scope: Continue PAR-92/7BA by removing pending-parent claim scans and child-first orphan duplicate scans while charging retained claim-index nodes to the existing bounded staging ledger.

implementation.declaredMembership: A sorted per-parent handle-to-source-slot index and staged-slot bitmap provide logarithmic membership and constant-time duplicate-slot checks while preserving the authoritative declaration list and callback order.
implementation.reverseClaims: An ordered map from child handle to ordered set of every pending parent that declares it replaces a full pending-parent scan. Deterministic tree lookup is logarithmic; handling a conflicting handle visits each actual claimant so existing group rejection can terminalize all involved owners.
implementation.orphanMembership: Each child-first orphan owner uses an ordered handle set for duplicate detection instead of scanning the staged orphan vertex vector.
implementation.rollback: Reverse claims are registered after parent state insertion and before source-frame staging. Partial claim registration rolls back on allocation/budget failure; pre-frame injection, frame-staging refusal, successful commit, terminalization, and orphan adoption release their corresponding modeled charges.

charged: declared-handle list nodes using sizeof(handle)+3 pointer widths as a conservative allocator-independent model
actual capacities of per-parent sorted handle indexes, staged-slot bitmaps, pending vertex vectors, and orphan vertex vectors
ordered reverse-claim map-key and owner-set node estimates
preparation scratch capacity bounded by both its local ceiling and remaining aggregate allowance
notCharged: pending/orphan unordered-map buckets and node overhead
allocator metadata and implementation-specific tree-node overhead beyond the charged model
budgetModel.qualification: The allowance is a retained-state budget estimate, not an RSS cap. Orphan vector growth preflights the old retained state plus planned new vector capacity and the incoming handle-set node as a transient peak.

cases: scrambled 512-child declaration order, exact slot lookup, and duplicate/missing refusal
four competing parents claim each of 512 child handles; all owners are queryable and removal returns the ordered index to zero bytes
one-byte reverse-index budget refuses without partial claims or changing the output byte counter
duplicate declared child slots create one owner claim per handle
existing vector/map growth and allocation-failure/retry controls

remaining: Index already-staged orphan identities globally so a later parent declaration can detect a foreign-owner orphan before final staged-state validation.
Decide whether to charge top-level pending/orphan unordered-map buckets and nodes and allocator overhead, or explicitly keep these outside the 256 MiB estimate.
Add complete stage/adopt/terminalize/lease rollback transcripts and verify all claims and charges survive retries without leaking or releasing another owner's claim.
No whole-reader speed, sanitizer, file-level support, native consumer, or external semantic claim is established.
